commentary.heading: Chip selloff drags Wall Street lower
commentary.body: US shares fell sharply on Monday as the selling in AI-linked stocks deepened. The S&P 500 dropped 1.92% to 7,416.6, its third straight loss, the Nasdaq Composite slid 2.49% to 24,509.8 and the Dow lost about 739 points (1.4%). Nvidia fell 4.1% ahead of its first results since Jensen Huang's resignation, with AMD, Broadcom and CoreWeave also lower. New US rules limiting remote access to advanced American chips through overseas data centres added to the pressure.

commentary.heading: Miners pull the ASX back
commentary.body: The ASX 200 eased 0.41% to 9,044.7 on Monday, its third loss in a row. Materials fell more than 2% as copper and iron ore prices slipped after weak Chinese data, with BHP down 2.8%, Rio Tinto 2.2% and Fortescue 2.9%. Seven of the 11 sectors still rose: technology gained about 1%, led by Xero (up 4.7%) and WiseTech (up 2.8%), and property and consumer staples were firmer.

commentary.heading: Mixed day in Asia and Europe
commentary.body: China's October figures disappointed, with industrial output growth of 4.8% and retail sales growth of just 0.4%. Mainland shares fell, the Shanghai Composite down 0.87% to 3,602.6 and the Shenzhen Component down 2.53% to 10,690.8 as AI stocks were sold. Hong Kong's Hang Seng bucked the trend, rising 0.49% to 23,753.8 on gains in banks and consumer names. The FTSE 100 slipped 0.19% to 10,881.6 as miners weighed.

commentary.heading: Central banks and inflation
commentary.body: There were no rate decisions on Monday. The RBA cash rate remains 4.85%, the US federal funds range 3.75–4.00% and the Bank of England rate 4.00%. In the UK, markets lifted expectations of a further Bank of England rise in December ahead of Wednesday's inflation figures.

commentary.heading: Bonds, oil and the Australian dollar
commentary.body: The US 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.13% from 5.15%, while the UK 10-year rose about 3 basis points to 5.37%, its highest since late October. Australia's 10-year was steady at 5.14%. Brent crude fell 3.5% to about US$92.44 a barrel. The Australian dollar slipped to about 67.4 US cents, near its lowest level since late January.

commentary.heading: What to watch
commentary.body: The RBA releases the minutes of its November meeting today. Overnight, the US publishes October retail sales and Nvidia reports quarterly results after the US close (Wednesday morning in Sydney). Wednesday brings UK October inflation, minutes from the Fed's October meeting and the pricing of Anthropic's share float, which is due to list on the Nasdaq on Thursday. Australian October jobs data follow on Thursday, along with Walmart and Alibaba results, and China sets its loan prime rates on Friday.
